Who We Are

More than a volunteer program.

The Kindred Network is a community-driven volunteer and cultural exchange project rooted in Busua, Ghana. We exist to give people an experience that goes beyond the typical — combining real impact with adventure, creativity, and genuine human connection.

Whether you're on a gap year, a long holiday, or simply looking for something meaningful, we bring together people from all backgrounds to build friendships, surf waves, share stories, and make a difference in a place that will stay with you long after you leave.

📍 Dixcove Methodist School & Future Leaders Academy
📚

Education · Dixcove, Ghana

Ghana Teaching Volunteers

Walk into the classrooms of Dixcove Methodist School and Future Leaders Academy — two pillars of education in the Dixcove community — and help shape the next generation. Work side by side with local teachers delivering English, maths, and creative lessons to children who are eager, curious, and full of life. No formal teaching experience needed. Just show up with energy, patience, and a genuine desire to connect.

  • Placements at Dixcove Methodist School & Future Leaders Academy
  • English, numeracy & creative arts support
  • Collaborative lesson planning with local teachers
  • Storytelling, drama & literacy workshops
  • Community school integration & cultural exchange

📍 Future Leaders Academy, Dixcove
🧒

Children & Community · Dixcove, Ghana

Child Care Program

Based at Future Leaders Academy in Dixcove, this program puts you right in the heart of early childhood development in coastal Ghana. Care for, play with, and nurture the youngest members of the community — children who light up every single day with laughter, creativity, and curiosity. You'll provide play-based learning, emotional support, and activities that give these kids the best possible start in life.

  • Early years placement at Future Leaders Academy
  • Play-based learning & sensory activities
  • Creative arts, music & movement sessions
  • Storytelling & early literacy support
  • Community family engagement & outreach

📍 Agona Government Hospital, Agona
🏥

Medical & Health · Agona, Ghana

Hospital Volunteering

Volunteer at Agona Government Hospital — a key healthcare facility serving the Agona community and surrounding areas of Ghana's Western Region. This is a rare and humbling opportunity to work alongside dedicated Ghanaian medical staff in a real clinical environment. Perfect for pre-med, nursing, public health, or any student with a passion for healthcare in Africa.

  • Placements at Agona Government Hospital
  • Ward & outpatient observation with clinical staff
  • Community health outreach & screening days
  • Health education & awareness workshops
  • Maternal & child health support programmes

📍 Busua Beach, Western Region
🌊🍳

Culture & Experience · Busua, Ghana

Surf & Ghanaian Culture Experience

This is Ghana at its fullest. Learn to ride the legendary waves of Busua Beach — one of West Africa's best surf spots — then head into the community to cook jollof, waakye, kelewele, and fresh palm wine with local families who have perfected these recipes for generations. Add photography walks, storytelling sessions, and bonfires on the beach, and you've got an experience that will genuinely change how you see the world.

  • Surf lessons on Busua Beach (beginner to intermediate)
  • Ghanaian cooking classes — dishes, snacks & local drinks
  • Photography walks & storytelling workshops
  • Cultural immersion with local Busua families
  • Beach bonfires, drumming & community events

The Process

How it works

01
🔍

Choose Your Program

Browse our four programs and pick the one that excites you. You can even combine programs across weeks. Not sure? Reach out and we'll guide you.

02
📋

Apply Online

Fill in our short application — takes about 10 minutes. Pay the registration fee ($70–$90) + €120 programme fee to secure your spot. No phone interviews, no hassle.

03
✈️

Prepare & Fly Out

We send a full info pack, volunteer handbook, and connect you with others travelling at the same time. Fly into Accra and we handle the rest.

04
🌊

Arrive & Live It

Our team meets you in Accra and takes you to Busua. Orientation, introductions, then the real adventure begins — surf, volunteer, connect, grow.

Why Trust Us

We're new. And that's a good thing.

Every great organisation starts somewhere. Here's why joining The Kindred Network now — at the very beginning — is something to be excited about, not worried about.

🌍

Built from the inside

This project was created by Anthony — someone who was born, raised, and lives in Busua. Not a company flying in from abroad to run programmes they've never experienced. The community connections, the school relationships, the hospital access — these are real, local, and personal.

🤝

Real placements. Real places.

Our volunteer placements are at institutions that have existed for years — Dixcove Methodist School, Future Leaders Academy, and Agona Government Hospital. These are not made-up programmes. You can look them up. They are real, active, and waiting for volunteers who care.

💰

Lower prices. More impact.

Because we are a small, community-run project with no big office overheads or corporate middlemen, we can keep costs low. More of your money goes directly into the community. We are intentionally priced below larger organisations like The Mighty Roar — same destination, deeper roots.

📩

Talk to us directly

Because we are small, you are not emailing a call centre. You are talking directly to the people running the programme — the same people who will welcome you when you arrive in Busua. Ask us anything. We will answer personally, honestly, and fast.

🏄

Busua is the destination

Busua is already one of West Africa's most beloved volunteer destinations — proven by organisations that have been running programmes here for years. The beach, the community, the culture — it's all here. We are simply offering a more personal, more affordable, and more authentic way to experience it.

⭐

Be our first. Shape everything.

The first volunteers to join The Kindred Network will receive our full personal attention, the best possible experience, and the chance to help shape what this project becomes. Your feedback, your photos, your story — they will help build something that lasts. You won't be one of hundreds. You'll be one of the first.

🔎

Full Transparency — No Surprises

We want to be upfront with you: The Kindred Network is a new project. We do not yet have hundreds of volunteer reviews or years of trip reports. What we do have is a genuine community in Busua, real school and hospital partners who have agreed to host volunteers, a co-founder who lives on the ground, and a total commitment to making every single volunteer's experience exceptional. We believe the best way to earn your trust is to be completely honest — and to deliver an experience that speaks for itself. If you have any questions at all, please email us directly. We will always respond.
